title: DatePicker date offset on Chrome/OSX - wrong dates, off by 1,000 years in some cases
body:
#### ALL software version info (bokeh, python, notebook, OS, browser, any other relevant packages)

Bokeh 12.16
Python 3.6.3 (Anaconda 3)
Spyder 3.2.8
Mac OSX High Sierra 10.13.5
Chrome 67.0.3396.87 (Official Build) (64-bit)

#### Description of expected behavior and the observed behavior

There is an offset of a day for min/max/value settings in the DatePicker widget

#### Complete, minimal, self-contained example code that reproduces the issue

```

from bokeh.layouts import (
    column,
    row,
)

from bokeh.models.widgets import (
    DatePicker,
)

from bokeh.plotting import output_file, reset_output, show


date0 = '1950-10-20'
datepicker0 = DatePicker(
    title=date0,
    min_date=date0,
    max_date=date0,
    value=date0,
)

date1 = '1969-12-31'
datepicker1 = DatePicker(
    title=date1,
    min_date=date1,
    max_date=date1,
    value=date1,
)

date2 = '1972-01-31'
datepicker2 = DatePicker(
    title=date2,
    min_date=date2,
    max_date=date2,
    value=date2,
)

date3 = '2018-10-20'
datepicker3 = DatePicker(
    title=date3,
    min_date=date3,
    max_date=date3,
    value=date3,
)

date4 = '1969-12-31'
datepicker4 = DatePicker(
    title=date4,
    min_date=date4,
    max_date=date4,
    value=date4,
)

date5 = '1989-07-14'
datepicker5 = DatePicker(
    title=date5,
    min_date=date5,
    max_date=date5,
    value=date5,
)

p = column(row(datepicker0, datepicker1, datepicker2), 
           row(datepicker3, datepicker4, datepicker5))
reset_output()
output_file('test.html')
show(p)


```
